name: Portland
tagline: No Sales Tax, Craft Culture, and Pacific Northwest Beauty
description: Portland offers a unique blend of progressive culture, no state sales tax, and easy access to the Pacific Northwest's stunning natural landscapes. The city is famous for its food cart scene, craft breweries, and bike-friendly infrastructure. While Oregon does have a state income tax, Portland's relatively moderate cost of living compared to Seattle or San Francisco, combined with its walkability and cultural richness, makes it an appealing FIRE destination for those who love gray skies and green landscapes.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – some urban challenges but generally safe neighborhoods
quickFacts.climate: Mild continental with wet winters and warm, dry summers

housing.description: A studio in an outer neighborhood like outer SE Portland, Beaverton, or Gresham — the metro's lowest-rent band

dining.description: Mostly home-cooked, with occasional food-cart meals and brewery happy hours

healthcare.description: Subsidized individual marketplace Silver at the sticky floor. Assumes an early retiree (45–55); older retirees budget more.

transportation.description: Car-light — a fare-capped TriMet pass in a highly bikeable city

entertainment.description: Forest Park, the Willamette trails, and free city recreation

1M.lifestyle: A careful but comfortable Pacific Northwest life. Housing is a studio in an outer neighborhood like outer SE Portland, Beaverton, or Gresham — the metro's lowest-rent band. Portland's genuinely usable transit (a fare-capped TriMet pass) and bike infrastructure keep a car off the budget entirely. Cooking at home is the norm, with food-cart meals and brewery happy hours as affordable outings, and Forest Park and the Willamette trails supply free recreation. No sales tax helps on everyday purchases, though Oregon's income tax is a headwind at any level.

3M.lifestyle: A relaxed, livable-city life in a one-bedroom in a walkable inner neighborhood like Hawthorne, Alberta, or Sellwood. Dining out regularly across Portland's dense food scene, a Subaru or EV for weekend trips to Mt. Hood or the coast, and a season ski pass all fit comfortably, alongside a solid private health plan through the OHSU network. This is one of the most livable tiers in the Pacific Northwest — comfortable and unhurried, with the mountains, coast, and wine country all an easy drive away.

10M.lifestyle: The top of Portland living, anchored by a luxury West Hills or Pearl District 2-bedroom with forest or city views. Near-daily fine dining across the city's chef-driven venues, a premium vehicle, full household help, and OHSU concierge medicine define the day-to-day, with first-class travel and premium season tickets at Moda Center on the calendar. The coast, Mt. Hood, and Willamette Valley wine country mean varied getaways without planning. Oregon's income tax is real at this level, but the quality of life is high.
